verdicts.title: Retrieval quality ties (recall@5 0.83 vs 0.85)
verdicts.body: Both run the same embedding model over the same corpus, so this is the expected result and the one worth having: adding push does not cost retrieval quality.

verdicts.title: Propagation coverage 64% (EventMem) vs 43% (mem0)
verdicts.body: EventMem spent 0 retrievals to get there; mem0 spent 11. The pull system was given one search per declared interest, which is a generous reading of how it is used, and it still has to know to go looking.

verdicts.title: Neither can exceed 64% on this corpus
verdicts.body: 16 of the 44 required deliveries name an agent that never declared an interest in that fact's topic, so no interest-based router can deliver them. Against only the 28 reachable ones, EventMem got 100% and mem0 got 57% - that is the number that isolates routing and transport from how well the interests were written.

verdicts.title: 40 facts reached an agent without it asking
verdicts.body: mem0 scores zero here by construction, not by failing: a passive store has no way to notify. This is a capability difference, not a performance one.

verdicts.title: Redis commands: 205 (EventMem) vs 115 (mem0)
verdicts.body: Counted from the server's own INFO commandstats. EventMem pays extra commands to push; mem0 pays them to search. Which is cheaper depends entirely on the read/write ratio of your workload.

verdicts.title: What this does not measure
verdicts.body: mem0 ran with infer=False, so its LLM fact-extraction, contradiction detection and memory-update logic were switched off. Those are its headline features and EventMem has no equivalent. This benchmark covers retrieval and propagation only.
